gen-gf-playpen-sans-deva-fs-plein: Plein reads clean and dependable, with a clear channel leading into each round letter, while Playpen Sans Deva scrawls above it like pen on paper. Its sans body keeps a few lines tidy.
gen-gf-playpen-sans-deva-fs-recia: Authoritative and sharp, Recia carries a faint swelling in its rounds that only shows up close. Recia's generous openings give Playpen Sans Deva, drawn with a technical pen's steady line, a surprisingly sturdy partner.
gen-gf-playpen-sans-deva-fs-rowan: Friendly and literary, Rowan has thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones. Playpen Sans Deva is best at casual, single-width handwriting, whereas Rowan does its best work with a classic serif's thick strokes leading the eye gently.
gen-gf-playpen-sans-deva-fs-spline-sans: Loose handwriting meets tidy modern lines. Spline Sans keeps wide gaps between curve ends and stems, and Playpen Sans Deva earns its keep when the words are big and short.
gen-gf-playpen-sans-deva-fs-synonym: Playpen Sans Deva writes its casual pen-and-paper letters across the top, with Synonym's plain stripe of constant ink in a sans body underneath. Handwriting and tidy sans make the difference here.
gen-gf-playpen-sans-deva-outfit: Approachable from the first word, Outfit bends its strokes like cable, with curves that finish well before they close. Outfit works nicely under Playpen Sans Deva if you give the body a little more size than feels necessary.
gen-gf-playpen-sans-deva-plus-jakarta-sa: Playpen Sans Deva cuts its terminals open so the counters flow outward, giving a relaxed hand. And Plus Jakarta Sans, monoline with curve endings kept well apart, can be sized up a touch to hold its own.
gen-gf-playpen-sans-deva-sora: Inviting handwriting from Playpen Sans Deva sits over Sora, whose curves turn corners without any pressure swell and keep the c and s widely parted. A plain sans meets a personal hand.
gen-gf-playpen-sans-hebrew-fs-amulya: Graceful curves that open outward lead Playpen Sans Hebrew, a casual hand with no swelling or tapering. But Amulya, a plain sans with generous gaps in its curves, handles the steadier, more modern work beneath.
gen-gf-playpen-sans-hebrew-fs-neco: Dignified Neco carries a measured swell from hairline to stem, under Playpen Sans Hebrew's bent-pipe-cleaner texture. And its letters never seem to pinch shut, so a longer stretch of serif text would feel steady.
